# Finite Character-DQI Readout: Mean And Tail Certificates

2026-10-18. Known DQI mechanism, LOCAL APPLICATION REVIEW PENDING.
CONDITIONAL on an exact source and exact verified unique decoder. This is
not a new quantum algorithm, a large quantum execution or a speedup claim.

## Question And Result

Does the fixed-input source ambiguity bound certify a finite useful score,
not just closeness to an unanalyzed ideal state? Yes, when an EXTRA observable
radius gives a sufficiently small radial Gram error. Source normalization
alone is insufficient, and the new certifier retains a counterexample.

At N127,K39,p=2^61-1, radius32, the certified normalized mean is about
0.9028547353515506, or114.66255 accepted positions. Conditional on the stated
receiver, one attempt has probability at least0.314586 of reaching110/127,
and0.050965 of reaching115/127. No binomial full-score law is assumed.

The saved same-input classical witness has109/127, but no matched runtime
comparison exists. The required finite decoder is still missing and the
published generic fixed-gap implementation has prohibitive-looking bounds.
It would be misleading to report this finite score certificate as an
implemented quantum advantage or to infer classical hardness from it.

## Problem, Algorithm And Costs

Reuse [the character source](PRIME_CHARACTER_CAPACITY_SOURCE.md): fixed public
quadratic-coset lists over p=3 mod4, strict or including zero; prime field,
distinct points1,...,N, degree<K. Local centered Fourier magnitudes are flat
away from zero. A radial superposition of sparse errors is mapped by the
K-row Vandermonde H to a coefficient-space syndrome. Verified unique decoding
and conditional erasure are followed by a finite-field Fourier readout.

The kernel is dual GRS of dimension N-K. Decoder rate is (N-K)/N and gap is
(K-ell)/N. The source, decoder, arithmetic, work-space uncomputation, QFT and
rotation errors all require actual compilation/resource accounting. Their
errors are NOT asserted to be zero for a physical implementation. An exact
mathematical receiver is the premise of the present certificates.

The proposed asymptotic gain remains known code-intersection sampling. The
new contribution to this repository is finite, fixed-input evaluation and
explicit rejection of invalid proof shortcuts, not an algorithmic novelty.

## Radial Near-Isometry

Let |j> be the normalized ambient sparse-error source of weight j. Its
nonzero entries on each support are products of the exact local ghat_i.
These radial states are orthonormal BEFORE syndrome coalescing. Their supports
at different j are disjoint, even with arbitrary public-shift phases.

Take the whole error ball of radius L<K and let A map |e> to |H e>, adding
amplitudes on collisions. This A is a mathematical coalescing map, NOT a free
quantum unitary. Put

    epsilon = max_(j<=L) epsilon_j,
    M = sum_(r<=L) C(N,r),
    delta = max(1,M-1)*epsilon.

For any unit radial superposition u, its bad mass b<=epsilon. Unique-good
and ambiguous-bad syndrome images have disjoint supports. The good image has
norm squared1-b and the bad image has norm squared at most M*b. Therefore

    1-epsilon <= ||A u||^2 <= 1+(M-1)*epsilon.

Writing G for the Gram matrix of the coalesced radial states proves

    ||G-I||_operator <= delta.

This is UNIFORM over radial coefficients, not a bound for only the particular
numerical filter that happened to look favorable. All source phases are
allowed; no random-input premise or favorable source selection is inserted.

## The Score Reaches One Extra Radius

Let q_j(x) be the elementary-symmetric degree-j polynomial in the centered
native predicates g_i(Q(a_i)), and phi_j=q_j/sqrt(C(N,j)). The known identity

    q1*q_j = (j+1)*q_(j+1) + (N-j+1)*q_(j-1) + beta*j*q_j,
    beta=(1-2rho)/sqrt(rho*(1-rho)),

is [Sun-Wootters, Lemma5.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.12357).
The normalized score operator in the AMBIENT radial basis has Jacobi matrix

    T[j,j] = rho+(1-2rho)*j/N,
    T[j,j+1] = sqrt(rho*(1-rho)*(j+1)*(N-j))/N.

The full matrix is the restriction of multiplication by a score in[0,1],
so it is a positive contraction. A source supported through ell is sent by
this observable through ell+1. Thus the near-isometry proof needs L=ell+1,
not just ell. With u supported through ell and ||u||=1,

    mu_ideal = (u^* G T u)/(u^* G u),
    mu0 = u^* T u,
    |mu_ideal-mu0| <= 2delta/(1-delta),  provided delta<1.

Here T*u is taken in the extended space through ell+1; no last-row term is
dropped. We use |u^*(G-I)T*u|<=delta and |u^*G*u-1|<=delta. We do NOT assume
that a truncated G*T commutes or is Hermitian on the entire extended space.
Only the stated source/observable bilinear identity is needed.

When 2ell+1<=K, the older exact RS-moment argument already determines every
needed term. That branch uses exact moments, not a false assertion that the
ENTIRE extended Gram matrix is identity. The artifact labels the two proof
methods separately. Outside that regime, ell+1>=K or delta>=1 is UNKNOWN,
even if a numerical Rayleigh quotient looks excellent.

## Rational Evaluation, Not A Floating Eigenvalue Claim

NumPy proposes positive radial weights from a tridiagonal eigenvector. The
actual filter uses saved DYADIC RATIONAL weights, normalized by their exact
squared norm. Each square-root matrix entry has an integer-isqrt rational
enclosure; signed weights use the correct interval direction. The certificate
is for that filter, not a formally certified optimum or eigenpair.

The native density rho=(p+eta)/(2p), eta+1 including zero and eta-1 strict,
is retained exactly. Neither is silently rounded to the balanced1/2 model.

The source pass separately bounds trace distance from the normalized full
ideal pushforward to the actual unique-herald output. Subtract its rational
square-root UPPER enclosure from the ideal mean lower bound. At radius32:

- Extended L33 Gram operator error<=1.027e-49.
- Ideal-mean correction<=2.054e-49.
- Herald-output TV<=7.257e-35, which dominates that correction.

These are exact mathematical-source guarantees-under-premises, NOT measured
gate errors. Any actual synthesis/decoder/QFT trace error must be added.

## Finite Tail Without Inventing A Distribution

Accepted count S takes integer values0,...,N. Given a normalized mean lower
bound mu, its threshold-k tail obeys

    Pr[S>=k] >= max(0,(N*mu-(k-1))/(N-(k-1))).

This is sharp given only that mean: failed mass can sit at k-1 and success
at N. Multiply by the source's herald-success floor for a per-attempt bound.
For fresh independent receiver preparations, repetition uses1-(1-p_success)^m.
Those repetitions are probabilities, not empirical confidence statements.
Serialized repeated bounds are conservative128-bit dyadic lower enclosures,
avoiding enormous decimal fractions without changing Python's global limits.

At ell32, reaching110 has floors0.314586 per attempt,0.779295 for4 attempts,
and0.997627 for16. Reaching115 has floor0.0509655 per attempt. There is no
matched cost certificate for any of these attempts. A zero lower tail at
another radius does NOT prove its actual tail is zero.

For degree76, modulus degree58, the sufficient field threshold falls from
756 bits to169 bits. The same fixed shifts/orientations in a declared

derivations.heading: Trace Bound And Its Dependencies
derivations.text:
Let U=P1 minus the geometric branch set, R=n+b branch values including
infinity. The local system attached to exterior^j V has rank C(n-1,j),
finite monodromy and weight0. It is tame because p>n implies p does not
divide n!. For j>=1 its geometric coinvariants vanish by the preceding
argument and characteristic-zero semisimplicity.

The imported cohomological facts are the compact-support trace formula,
Hc0 vanishing on this affine curve, the coinvariant description of Hc2,
the tame Euler-characteristic formula and the weight<=1 bound for Hc1.
See Fouvry-Kowalski-Michel's
[Trace functions over finite fields and applications](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~kowalski/elements.pdf),
Chapter4, Theorem4.1.4, Propositions4.1.5/4.1.6 and Theorems4.1.7/4.1.9
(PDF pages33-35; printed pages31-33), draft dated December3,2014. The notes
are an exposition with some proof TODOs, not an
independent review of this application. Finite monodromy supplies weight0;
no unspecified conductor constant is substituted for an explicit bound.
Retrieved PDF SHA256:
`40dfd0f77b43e5f79ac7304695efb3a6d2d7ed23c3f14a5dde8468d80a0a6e43`.

Thus for each j>=1, Hc0=Hc2=0 and the Swan conductors vanish. Consequently

    dim Hc1(U, exterior^j V) = (R-2)*C(n-1,j),
    |sum_(v in U(Fp)) chi_j(Frob_v)|
       <= (R-2)*C(n-1,j)*sqrt(p).

At unramified fibers Frobenius cycle type equals the degrees of the distinct
irreducible factors of f-vg. Summing the exact indicator, and keeping the
trivial j=0 term SEPARATE, proves

    n*I = #U(Fp) + sum_(j=1)^(n-1) (-1)^j sum_v chi_j(Frob_v),
    #U(Fp) >= p+1-R,
    A = (R-2)*(2^(n-1)-1),
    I/p >= max(0, (p+1-R-A*ceil(sqrt(p)))/(n*p)).

All geometric branch points are charged, even those not rational. Infinity
is already removed; there is no second branch-fiber subtraction by n!.
The ceil square root is intentionally pessimistic. No floating confidence
bound or fixed-degree hidden constant enters this count.

Keep the old twist bound too: for n4,p10007 it is actually stronger. Selecting
the maximum of TWO deterministic proved-under-premises bounds is legitimate;
it is not multiple-testing or selection by observed success.

notes.self_check:
1. A general class function need not have zero mean. The trivial character
   supplies #U(Fp); omitting it would destroy the calculation. The class
   averages and exact identity are checked independently.
2. Arithmetic/geometric monodromy mismatch could destroy the density. The
   preceding Morse proof must really give geometric S_n. The A_n test shows
   a concrete failure of the invariant premise, not just a warning string.
3. Wild ramification adds Swan terms. Characteristic restrictions remain
   mandatory; a nominal positive numeric bound cannot override geometry.
4. The trace theorem bounds Hc1, not just a smooth compact curve. Compact
   supports, missing branch values, Hc2 coinvariants, and weight0 input are
   stated explicitly. These applications still need independent review.
5. A finite seeded success cannot prove a fixed-input distributional claim.
   Full small-field factorizations calibrate each trace, but they are NOT
   the large-field algorithm or a replacement for the trace proof.
6. Large-field lifting changes OPI. No descent to the original61-bit input,
   all-field solver, low-rate solver or higher-character extension follows.
7. No quantum source, decoder or readout was discovered. The benefit is a
   stronger classical falsifier that narrows where research can credibly
   seek an advantage, not an assertion of a Shor-level discovery.

# Fixed-Input OPI: A Smaller Classical Field-Size Guarantee

2026-10-18. LOCAL APPLICATION REVIEW PENDING. No novelty, quantum algorithm,
all-field dequantization or independently accepted proof is claimed.

## Scientific Question And Outcome

Can the verified Morse norm solver avoid a factorial-genus error when
counting irreducible fibers? YES under the local trace argument below.
For degree76, modulus degree58, the sufficient field threshold falls from
756 bits to169 bits. The same fixed shifts/orientations in a declared
192-bit prime field now give a strict perfect127/127 witness after24 fibers.
The old twist bound is zero in that field. This is a genuinely enlarged
fixed-input guarantee, not an empirical seed-success estimate.

The original61-bit large source still has ZERO lower bound under both
methods. A lift to a different field does not solve or give a probability
guarantee for that original input. No field-descent claim is made.

## Problem And Mechanism

Use the explicit prime-field quadratic-coset OPI model in
[the Morse solver](PRIME_CHARACTER_MORSE_ATTACK.md): N distinct points,
public shifts, two orientations, verified nonsquare, degree<K, optional
strict exclusion of zero. The stored implementation uses points1,...,N.
Choose majority group A, minority B of size b, even n=2*floor((K-1)/2).
Require |A|<K, n>=4, n-b>=3 and p>max(n+b-1,2N).

Reuse the public unit-residue arithmetic progression and two-parameter
Morse perturbation. CHECK coprimality, simple poles, simple critical points
AND distinct critical values over the algebraic closure. The existing local
tame inertia argument gives geometric/arithmetic S_n, not merely A_n.
Then f-vg irreducible implies an actual polynomial norm, which yields the
native OPI witness; strict Cayley rotations exclude all forbidden zeros.
Nothing changes in the norm construction, source model or final verifier.

The classical baseline is the existing norm/twist solver. The prospective
quantum opening was efficient perfect intersection on these explicit lists;
an expected-polynomial classical solver removes that opening in this promised
regime. This does NOT address arbitrary oracle lists or low-rate instances.

## Exact Cycle Indicator

Let V be the (n-1)-dimensional characteristic-zero standard representation
of S_n and sigma have cycle lengths ell_1,...,ell_c. Then

    det(1-t*sigma | V) = product_i(1-t^ell_i)/(1-t).

At t=1 this equals n for an n-cycle and0 when there are at least two cycles.
The determinant/exterior-power identity therefore gives the EXACT identity

    n*1_(n-cycle)(sigma)
       = sum_(j=0)^(n-1) (-1)^j chi_j(sigma),
    chi_j(sigma) = Tr(sigma | exterior^j V).

The implementation computes chi_j from the integer polynomial
product_i(1-(-z)^ell_i)/(1+z), without a character-table library. This is used
only for small independent controls, not by the large-input solver.

No nontrivial exterior power has S_n-invariants. An elementary check avoids
assuming a full irreducible-character classification: in the basis
e_i-e_n, the subgroup S_(n-1) permutes the basis. For j>=2, any exterior
basis element contains two indices; swapping those indices fixes its support
and negates its coefficient, so every invariant coefficient is zero. For
j=1 the S_(n-1)-invariant vector is a multiple of sum_(i<n)(e_i-e_n), which
is not fixed by swapping1 with n. Only exterior^0 has an invariant line.

This argument FAILS on A_n: the top exterior power is sign and becomes
trivial. The tests explicitly reproduce that failure. Dropping the full
geometric S_n premise would silently lose the leading-term calculation.

## Trace Bound And Its Dependencies

Let U=P1 minus the geometric branch set, R=n+b branch values including
infinity. The local system attached to exterior^j V has rank C(n-1,j),
finite monodromy and weight0. It is tame because p>n implies p does not
divide n!. For j>=1 its geometric coinvariants vanish by the preceding
argument and characteristic-zero semisimplicity.

The imported cohomological facts are the compact-support trace formula,
Hc0 vanishing on this affine curve, the coinvariant description of Hc2,
the tame Euler-characteristic formula and the weight<=1 bound for Hc1.
See Fouvry-Kowalski-Michel's
[Trace functions over finite fields and applications](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~kowalski/elements.pdf),
Chapter4, Theorem4.1.4, Propositions4.1.5/4.1.6 and Theorems4.1.7/4.1.9
(PDF pages33-35; printed pages31-33), draft dated December3,2014. The notes
are an exposition with some proof TODOs, not an
independent review of this application. Finite monodromy supplies weight0;
no unspecified conductor constant is substituted for an explicit bound.
Retrieved PDF SHA256:
`40dfd0f77b43e5f79ac7304695efb3a6d2d7ed23c3f14a5dde8468d80a0a6e43`.

Thus for each j>=1, Hc0=Hc2=0 and the Swan conductors vanish. Consequently

    dim Hc1(U, exterior^j V) = (R-2)*C(n-1,j),
    |sum_(v in U(Fp)) chi_j(Frob_v)|
       <= (R-2)*C(n-1,j)*sqrt(p).

At unramified fibers Frobenius cycle type equals the degrees of the distinct
irreducible factors of f-vg. Summing the exact indicator, and keeping the
trivial j=0 term SEPARATE, proves

    n*I = #U(Fp) + sum_(j=1)^(n-1) (-1)^j sum_v chi_j(Frob_v),
    #U(Fp) >= p+1-R,
    A = (R-2)*(2^(n-1)-1),
    I/p >= max(0, (p+1-R-A*ceil(sqrt(p)))/(n*p)).

All geometric branch points are charged, even those not rational. Infinity
is already removed; there is no second branch-fiber subtraction by n!.
The ceil square root is intentionally pessimistic. No floating confidence
bound or fixed-degree hidden constant enters this count.

Keep the old twist bound too: for n4,p10007 it is actually stronger. Selecting
the maximum of TWO deterministic proved-under-premises bounds is legitimate;
it is not multiple-testing or selection by observed success.

## Uniform Field Regime And Cost

A sufficient condition for the new fiber success rate>=1/(2n) is

    p >= max(16*A^2, 4*(R+A)).

Indeed A*sqrt(p)<=p/4, A*ceil(sqrt(p))<=p/4+A, and R+A<=p/4.
Add p>=2*D_bad from the existing generic Morse-parameter bound to give
expected<=2 geometry trials, where D_bad=(2d-2)*(n+d+1), d=n+b-1.
Every actual geometry is still verified; the numeric field bound alone
cannot certify S_n or permit a non-Morse input to enter the norm stage.

The threshold has O(n+log(n+b)) bits instead of O(n log n). The coefficient
2^(n-1)-1 has only n bits. No exponential-rank object, cohomology complex,
cover or group enumeration is constructed. The algorithm uses expected
polynomially many exact finite-field interpolations/resultants,
irreducibility/factorization operations and norm rotations, in N and log p.
We import standard randomized finite-field factorization complexity; the
implementation does not give certified low-level bit-operation budgets.

For a VERIFIED fixed geometry, fresh independent uniform fibers can be
amplified. A seeded replay is NOT an IID confidence certificate. The live
control's1672-fiber cap at n76 has failure<=2^-10 under the uniform-coin
premise, not because this one seeded execution succeeded.

## Executed Evidence

- All conjugacy classes for n2 through12: exact cycle indicator, correct
  n-cycle count, character/rank bounds and zero nontrivial invariant averages.
- Independent standard-representation matrix determinant with cycle type3,2,1.
- A_n countermodel: the top exterior invariant reappears as predicted.
- Full charged quartic fibers over p29,101,1009,10007:8,40,264,2528
  irreducible fibers. Factorization-derived character sums independently
  obey the indicator and each proposed cohomological error bound. At10007,
  two finite branch values are rational; #U(Fp)=10005, not p or p+1.
- The DECLARED prime p=2^192-2^64-1 retains all127 original shifts and
  orientations from the strict seed29 input. FLINT verifies primality and
  the chosen coset multiplier. One Morse geometry,24 charged fiber tests,
  strict127/127 witness, positive trace bound, zero old twist bound.
- The original61-bit source remains field-guarded, not promoted to hard
  or unsatisfiable. The old quartic bound wins when it should.

## Attempts To Disprove It And Remaining Debt

1. A general class function need not have zero mean. The trivial character
   supplies #U(Fp); omitting it would destroy the calculation. The class
   averages and exact identity are checked independently.
2. Arithmetic/geometric monodromy mismatch could destroy the density. The
   preceding Morse proof must really give geometric S_n. The A_n test shows
   a concrete failure of the invariant premise, not just a warning string.
3. Wild ramification adds Swan terms. Characteristic restrictions remain
   mandatory; a nominal positive numeric bound cannot override geometry.
4. The trace theorem bounds Hc1, not just a smooth compact curve. Compact
   supports, missing branch values, Hc2 coinvariants, and weight0 input are
   stated explicitly. These applications still need independent review.
5. A finite seeded success cannot prove a fixed-input distributional claim.
   Full small-field factorizations calibrate each trace, but they are NOT
   the large-field algorithm or a replacement for the trace proof.
6. Large-field lifting changes OPI. No descent to the original61-bit input,
   all-field solver, low-rate solver or higher-character extension follows.
7. No quantum source, decoder or readout was discovered. The benefit is a
   stronger classical falsifier that narrows where research can credibly
   seek an advantage, not an assertion of a Shor-level discovery.

## Next Decision

Do not keep refining high-rate norm thresholds by inertia. The original
low-rate K39 model fails the majority-degree budget before this trace bound
is relevant. The next constructive question should attack that DIFFERENT
degree barrier or compare an independent source/code mechanism. Merely
testing another seed/prime or removing another constant is not enough.

```text
python theorems/prime_character_exterior_bound.py --write
python -m pytest -q tests/test_prime_character_exterior_bound.py
```

# Low-Rate Character OPI: Source And Coherent Ambiguity

2026-10-18. KNOWN DQI mechanism instantiated analytically; LOCAL APPLICATION
REVIEW PENDING. No new algorithm, quantum speedup, classical hardness or
executed large quantum decoder is claimed.

## Question And Decision

For the explicit low-rate prime-character model, can we control source-error
ambiguity beyond half the minimum distance without randomizing input shifts?
YES for the flat-spectrum primes below. But negligible ambiguity is NOT an
efficient decoder. The full capacity-decoding paper has been inspected past
its abstract, and its finite/running-time qualifications matter severely.

The concrete route is known DQI: generate sparse Fourier errors, compute a
public RS syndrome, coherently erase uniquely decodable errors, then perform
Fourier readout. The goal is a genuine end-to-end comparison on compact public
lists, not an oracle separation. Existing high-rate norm solvers do not meet
the degree budget at N127,K39; existing classical jet repair reaches109/127.
Neither that finite score nor non-applicability proves asymptotic hardness.

The published capacity-DQI score law is an asymptotic target, not the finite
mean/tail of the newly considered radius32 state. The latter is NOT certified
here. No new speedup candidate is admitted on the basis of these source bounds.

FOLLOW-UP: [finite readout certificates](PRIME_CHARACTER_FINITE_READOUT.md)
now supply a conditional finite mean/tail by paying for the observable's
EXTRA radius. This supersedes the missing finite-score status above, not the
unimplemented decoder/circuit or absent runtime advantage.

## Exact Local Source

Let chi be the quadratic character, with chi(0)=0. Write eta=+1 for lists
including zero, eta=-1 for strict lists. For public shift t_i and orientation
sigma_i, the native predicate has density rho=(p+eta)/(2p). Its centered,
unit-variance function is

    g_i(x) = [p*(-1)^sigma_i*chi(x-t_i)
                 +eta*(p*1_(x=t_i)-1)]/sqrt(p^2-1).

With Fourier convention ghat(xi)=E_x g(x)*exp(-2pi*i*xi*x/p), ghat(0)=0.
For xi!=0 the exact formula is

    ghat_i(xi) = exp(-2pi*i*xi*t_i/p)
       *[eta+(-1)^sigma_i*chi(-xi)*tau_p]/sqrt(p^2-1),
    tau_p = sum_x chi(x)*exp(2pi*i*x/p).

The classical quadratic Gauss evaluation gives tau_p=i*sqrt(p) at p=3 mod4.
See [Murty-Pathak, Theorem1.1](https://www.cmi.ac.in/~siddhi/Quadratic_Gauss_Sum.pdf).
Consequently EVERY nonzero Fourier probability is exactly1/(p-1), regardless
of shifts, orientations and zero convention. The phases remain essential;
uniform classical error samples are not a replacement for their interference.

At p=1 mod4, tau_p is real and these magnitudes are NOT flat. The p5 control
has probability spread sqrt(5)/6. The flat-source wrapper rejects that case
instead of silently importing an IID-uniform error premise.

One may construct a uniform nonzero register by a binary interval-prefix
rotation tree, followed by incrementing its uniform0,...,p-2 value. Only one
boundary prefix per bit needs a non-Hadamard split; controlled gates give
polynomial work in log p. Apply the public shift phase and a two-valued phase
controlled by reversible Legendre computation, then uncompute work bits.
Controlled versions can act on an error-support superposition. Approximate
rotations, modular arithmetic and the support/weight preparation must all be
compiled and charged; this pass does NOT implement that scalable circuit.
Heralding a separate uncontrolled rejection coin for each active support
wire would require a coherence analysis, not a free source shortcut.

## Correct Code And Input Model

Use H[j,i]=a_i^j for j=0,...,K-1, so H maps N error symbols to K syndrome
symbols. Any K columns are independent. Its kernel is the DUAL GRS code of
dimension N-K and minimum distance K+1. This H is not the N-K-row parity
matrix used by the separate affine-quadrics exporter.

Syndrome decoding reduces to ordinary RS list decoding: solve H*y=s publicly,
then recover kernel codewords near y. Known nonzero GRS column multipliers
convert them to ordinary RS while preserving Hamming distance. Thus decoder
rate is (N-K)/N, NOT K/N; radius ell has capacity gap (K-ell)/N. No secret
shift or hidden code is supplied.

For a fixed support S of size j, nonzero error values are independent uniform
in Fp*. This describes basis probabilities of the coherent error state; it
does not assume that public t_i are random. Different coordinates' phases
may be arbitrary. Radial weight superpositions use uniform supports at each
weight, exactly as in the known DQI source.

## Ambiguity Against The Entire Ball

Fix S, |S|=j<=ell<K, and competitor support T of size r<=ell. Let h=|S cap T|.
If |S union T|<=K, MDS independence forbids a distinct collision with both
supports exact/nonzero. Otherwise the intersection of the two syndrome
subspaces has dimension j+r-K. Each support map is injective. At most
p^(j+r-K)-1 possible nonzero source vectors can collide on that T.

The number of such supports at overlap h is C(j,h)*C(N-j,r-h). Therefore

    epsilon_j <= min(1,
      sum_(r=0)^ell sum_h C(j,h)*C(N-j,r-h)
        *(p^(j+r-K)-1)/(p-1)^j ),

where only j+r>K and max(0,j+r-N)<=h<=min(j,r,j+r-K-1) contribute.
Set epsilon=max_j epsilon_j. It bounds bad source mass for ANY normalized
radial weights. All arithmetic is exact, polynomial-size combinatorial
counting; no field/error table is built for the large records.

Equal-weight-only testing would be wrong: a retained weight5 kernel vector
over F7 splits into colliding errors of weights2 and3. Unique-distance checks
at radius2 would miss that radius3 competitor. Every bound here counts the
whole radius-ell ball, including all smaller weights.

## Coherent Error Is Not Bad Mass

Let A coalesce all radius-ell errors with the same syndrome. At most one
error per support maps to any syndrome, so each fiber has size at most

    M=sum_(r=0)^ell C(N,r).

This exponential COUNT is used as an O(N)-bit integer, not enumerated by the
large-input computation. In a calibration, the whole ball really is enumerated
and explicitly charged.

Decompose a normalized source into unique-good and ambiguous-bad vectors.
Their syndrome images G and B have DISJOINT supports. If actual bad mass is
epsilon_actual<=epsilon, then ||G||^2=1-epsilon_actual and
||B||^2<=M*epsilon_actual by Cauchy-Schwarz. Postselecting a coherent unique
decoder's success flag yields G/||G||, not the unheralded full ideal state.
If epsilon<1 the ideal state (G+B)/||G+B|| is well defined, and

    P(unique herald)>=1-epsilon,
    trace_distance^2 <= M*epsilon/(1-epsilon+M*epsilon).

The same bound controls TV after Fourier readout. An explicit aligned M22,
epsilon1/100 countercontrol saturates this pure-distance bound: error can be
over40 times the failed source mass. Do not charge only epsilon as output TV.
This does NOT supply a decoder, a gate budget, or an independent approximation
to arbitrary normalized-coset sampling.

## What The Full Decoder Paper Actually Supplies

[Dao-Kominers-Thaler](https://quangvdao.github.io/papers/authored/reed-solomon-codes-beyond-johnson.pdf),
Section9.1 and Theorem9.16, gives deterministic fixed-gap decoding in the
binary input size, with explicit field-presentation premises. Its stated
runtime is B_delta*N^O(exp(1.5/delta))*polylog(p). Finite parameters depend
on delta; "polynomial" does not mean a practical circuit. Only relevant
statements and recovery construction were audited, not the entire145-page
proof or its Lean development.

For delta<6/25, equation87 and Theorem6.8 have a length threshold at least the
derivative order d=ceil(exp(1.5/delta))>500. The generic finite certificate
therefore cannot be applied directly at N127. Its bounded-length fallback
is exact but is not a useful gate-budget argument. A sharper rate-specific
first-order certificate or an actual alternative decoder would need separate
parameters and implementation; no hidden initial field-value enumeration is
allowed. Prime-field arithmetic supplies the needed field representation,
but does not remove that recovery cost.

`b67c188ec477b6063caf9c1c06b214c71e358ff09b9517adcdb1db212ea2700a`.

# OPI Filter Tails Without An Exponential State

2026-10-17. Local moment extension and certificates, review pending. Known
DQI mechanism; no new quantum algorithm, hardness result or cost separation.

## The Scientific Gap

The [cubic-target controls](EXPLICIT_CUBIC_OPI.md) have classical best-of-four
scores above a known quantum mean. That is not a comparison of success
probabilities. The next question is whether we can bound the NATIVE filter
tail without assuming a convenient full score distribution or enumerating
all 2^(Kt) RS messages.

## Exact Moment Argument

Let S be the number of accepted coordinates for a UNIFORM RS message. Any
K positions of a dimension-K RS code are independent uniform field symbols,
by the Vandermonde interpolation map. Every fixed balanced predicate then
gives a fair bit at those positions. Consequently E[Q(S)] equals the
Binomial(N,1/2) expectation for every polynomial Q of degree at most K.
No IID predicate ensemble or oracle distribution is needed for this fact.

Use a degree-ell filter P(S). Its ideal DQI probability on a message is
proportional to P(S)^2. The normalization and r-th score moment are therefore
exactly known whenever 2 ell+r <= K. With K_j the unnormalized Krawtchouk
polynomials, choose an EXPLICIT rational filter

```
P(s) = sum_j b_j K_j(s),   b_j rational
Z = sum_j b_j^2 * C(N,j)
E_filtered[(S/N)^r]
  = sum_s C(N,s)/2^N * P(s)^2 * (s/N)^r / Z.
```

The code approximates the known positive mean-filter coefficients with exact
dyadic inverse-square-root factors. It certifies THIS rational polynomial,
not an exactly optimal eigenvector. All sums and moments are rational.
The sum has only N+1 terms, not 2^(Kt) messages.

CRITICAL: the expression on the right computes the permitted moments, NOT
the full native score distribution. Beyond the degree cutoff, code relations
can radically change the distribution. The countercontrol K=1 with identical
predicates has native score either zero or N, not a binomial distribution.
The maximum mean filter at K=39,ell=19 allows only ONE certified moment.
Claiming its variance from the binomial surrogate would be an error.

The [known DQI score/state construction, Appendix A](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02145v2#A1)
supplies the filter mechanism and distance context. The higher-moment identity
here follows from the explicit interpolation argument; no novelty claim is made.

## Independently Verifiable Tail Bounds

For a threshold k, a numerical moment LP proposes coefficients of a polynomial
q(x) below 1[S>=k] on the finite support x=s/N. Every coefficient is converted
to a rational number. An EXACT support-wide constant repair removes any
numerical infeasibility. The code then verifies

```
q_lower(s/N) <= 1[s>=k] <= q_upper(s/N),   s=0,...,N.
```

Taking certified moment expectations gives rational lower and upper bounds.
No numerical LP optimum is trusted or claimed certified. Failed numerical
optimization gives valid trivial [0,1] bounds, not a research finding.
The saved dual polynomials are checked without rerunning the numerical solver.
One, four and sixteen ideal independent executions have outward-rounded
dyadic success bounds. These are ATTEMPT counts, not matched gate budgets.
An approximate compiled circuit would need its own trace-error allowance.

## Live Findings

At N=127,K=39:

| Filter degree | Certified moments | Mean | Guaranteed Pr[S>=102] |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 | 7 | 0.789980 | >=0.022620 |
| 18 | 3 | 0.808256 | >=0.178033 |
| 19 | 1 | 0.816830 | >=0.105285 |

For degree19, Pr[S>=104] >=0.0307255 for EVERY balanced input of the stated
RS form, including the two compact cubic instances. Degree18 also gives a
positive lower bound at104. These are not empirically measured probabilities.
At105 the implemented moment certificates give zero as the lower bound:
UNKNOWN, not zero actual success. Upper bounds remain broad. The lower-degree
filter's better certified102 tail is not proof that its actual tail is better;
the degree19 moment relaxation has less information.

Thus classical105/127 and104/127 remain verified witnesses but do NOT kill
the quantum tail. Conversely, a universal known-algorithm tail guarantee does
not make the explicit input family classically hard, nor supply a new algorithm.
The relevant unresolved comparison is success at a shared threshold under a
charged full-work budget, with stronger adaptive classical attacks retained.

## Run And Review

```
python theorems/opi_filter_tail_certificate.py --write
python -m pytest tests/test_opi_filter_tail_certificate.py -q -W error::RuntimeWarning
```

The report binds its producer, both OPI dependencies and cubic input artifact
by SHA256. Tests compare ALL allowed moments and tail bounds against complete
small native-field enumeration; reject forbidden higher moments, corrupted
dual polynomials and repetition arithmetic; and check numerical-failure and
infeasible-dual countercontrols. This validates the implementation, not the
unreviewed mathematical premises or an actual coherent decoder/filter.

Do not add mean/tail labels to a speedup registry entry. CLI exposure and
production regressions are mechanical follow-up. A new scientific pass needs
an adaptive code-aware classical mechanism, a constructive quantum resource
improvement, or an independent higher-upside algorithmic route, not more
filter/seed scans of these already understood finite controls.
